```{r Read in cleaned data}
df <- fread()
```

# Hyp: It is expected that trait empathy measures (Interpersonal Reactivity Index, Empathy Index) at baseline will be predictive of empathy in the experience sampling surveys.
  # Appears to be true in a variety of ways
# Hyp: It is predicted that scores on the empathy selection task will be associated with greater reported opportunities to empathize.
  # Some evidence but effect did not survive FDR adjustment

```{r Predicting daily empathy from trait empathy}

###SITES###
summaryh(glmer(formula = E_Opp ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id), data = df, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=100000))))
# b = 0.14, SE = 0.10, z(7086) = 1.42, p = .155, r = 0.04
summaryh(glmer(formula = E ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=100000))))
# b = 0.62, SE = 0.18, z(1332) = 3.44, p < .001, r = 0.17
summaryh(glmer(formula = PT ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=100000))))
###  b = 0.21, SE = 0.17, z(1166) = 1.25, p = .210, r = 0.06
summaryh(glmer(formula = ES ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df, family = binomial))
#  b = 0.14, SE = 0.17, z(1166) = 0.86, p = .390, r = 0.04
summaryh(glmer(formula = comp ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id), data = df, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=100000))))
# b = 0.85, SE = 0.40, z(1167) = 2.13, p = .033, r = 0.23
summaryh(lmer(formula = PT_extent ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df))
#  b = 0.26, SE = 0.08, t(170) = 3.25, p = .001, r = 0.24 
summary(lmer(formula = ES_extent ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df))
# b = 0.23, SE = 0.07, t(171) = 3.38, p = 0.000905, r = 0.25
summary(lmer(formula = comp_extent ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df))
# b = 0.25, SE = 0.06, t(177) = 4.18, p = 4.62e-05, r = 0.30
summary(lmer(formula = PT_conf ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df))
# b = 0.21, SE = 0.06, t(165) = 3.38, p = .00091, r = 0.25
summaryh(lmer(formula = ES_conf ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df))
# b = 0.09, SE = 0.06, t(162) = 1.50, p = .135, r = 0.12
summaryh(lmer(formula = comp_conf ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df))
#  b = 0.15, SE = 0.06, t(162) = 2.65, p = .009, r = 0.20
summaryh(lmer(formula = PT_diff ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df))
# b = -0.19, SE = 0.10, t(170) = -1.93, p = .055, r = 0.15
summaryh(lmer(formula = comp_diff ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df))
#  b = -0.19, SE = 0.10, t(169) = -1.97, p = .051, r = 0.15
summaryh(lmer(formula = ES_diff ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=100000))))
# b = -0.21, SE = 0.09, t(196) = -2.31, p = .022, r = 0.16
summary(lmer(formula = ExtentAvg_score ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df))
# b = 0.26, SE = 0.06, t(186) = 4.49, p = .0000126, r = 0.31
summaryh(lmer(formula = DiffAvg_score ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df))
#   b = -0.20, SE = 0.08, t(195) = -2.51, p = .013, r = 0.18
summaryh(lmer(formula = ConfAvg_score ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df))
# b = 0.16, SE = 0.06, t(174) = 2.89, p = .004, r = 0.21
summaryh(lmer(formula = T_extentAvg ~  SITES_C + (1|User_Id/Survey_Day), data = df))
# b = 0.07, SE = 0.07, t(153) = 1.06, p = .290, r = 0.09 


#Make vectors of t scores, p scores, variable names. MAKE SURE THEY MATCH.
tSITESdaily <- c(1.42, 3.44, 1.25, 0.86, 2.13, 3.25, 3.38, 4.18, 3.38, 1.50, 2.65, -1.93, -1.97, -2.31, 4.49, -2.51, 2.89, 1.06)
pSITES <- c(0.155, 0.00058, 0.210, 0.390, 0.033, 0.001, 0.000905, 0.0000462, 0.00091, 0.135, 0.009, 0.055, 0.051, 0.022, 0.0000126, 0.013, 0.004, 0.290)
Daily_Empathy_Component <- c("Empathy Opportunity", "Empathy", "Perspective Taking", "Emotion Sharing", "Compassion", "Pers. Taking Extent", "Emotion Sharing Extent", "Compassion Extent", "PT Confidence", "ES Confidence", "Compassion Confidence", "Perpsective Taking Difficulty", "Emotion Sharing Difficulty",  "Compassion Difficulty", "Extent Empathy", "Difficulty Empathy", "Confidence Empathy", "Target of Empathy Extent")

#adjust p values
adjp_SITES <- p.adjust(pSITES, method = "fdr", n = length(pSITES)) %>% round(4)
#Make a data frame object with these as columns
adjp_SITESTbl_df <- data.frame(Daily_Empathy_Component, tSITESdaily, adjp_SITES)
# Make a table
tab_df(adjp_SITESTbl_df, title = "Daily Empathy by Single Item Trait Empathy Scale", col.header = c("Daily Empathy Variable", "z or t score", "Adjusted P value"), footnote = "Table . Shows t scores and FDR adjusted p values for daily empathy variables predicted by centered SITES scores nested within participant and day.", show.footnote = TRUE, alternate.rows = TRUE)

#Once you save the output from viewer:
rm(tSITESdaily, pSITES, pSITES, adjp_SITES, adjp_SITESTbl_df)


#SITES is predictive of extent of empathy in daily life. Looking at components independently it is associated with comp extent only.
```

-	Hyp: We will test if empathy is associated with higher subjective well-being.

  Running all of our trait empathy subscales as predictors in a full model, we found no significant association between subjective well-being and trait empathy. It is worth noting that, because our predictors are correlated, the results from the full model do not represent the zero order correlation for all variables. Using each subscale as a single predictor, only personal distress from the interpersonal reactivity reached significance (t =, p =). This provides support for the idea that certain forms of empathy, specifically the tendency to feel emotional distress when presented with the suffering of others, can have a negative impact on subjective well-being. 
  Previous research (Shiffman, 2008, Runyam, 2018) suggests that experience sampling measures may be able to uncover associations that retrospective measures miss. Therefore, we tested whether participant averages of the extent to which they felt distress, shared emotions, took perspective, and felt compassion throughout the course of the week, would be predictive of participants average subjective well-being. As our empathy in daily life variables were correlared, we tested each component individually.  


-      Hyp: It is predicted that higher empathy confidence ratings will be associated with more empathy.
-      Hyp: It is predicted that higher empathy difficulty ratings will be associated with less empathy. 

  Previous research completed in the lab with the empathy selection task provides evidence that individuals with higher reported confidence were more likely to empathize when given the choice. Therefore, we predicted increased confidence ratings of the accuracy of emotion sharing, perspective taking, and compassion in everyday life would be associated with increased empathizing in everyday life. Prior research with the empathy selection task has also demonstrated that reported difficulty is negatively associated with empathy, so we predicted a similar relationship in our everyday empathy variables.

  We found agreeableness ( ) and extraversion ( ) were both predictive of increased extent of empathy in daily life. However, we did  not find a significant link between openness and empathy. Though not preregistered, we performed an exploratory model predicting average extent of everyday empathy from conscientousness, and found it was significant ( ). Neuroticism was, as predicted, negatively associated with the average extent of empathy in daily life.

We will test the relationship between empathy at time 1 and prosocial behaviour and subjective well-being at time 2. We will examine whether trait empathy measures predict self-reports of emotion sharing, perspective taking, and compassion. We will examine the correlations between emotion sharing, perspective taking, and compassion. We will provide descriptive statistics about how often people experience opportunities to empathize, and how often they actually empathize.
